name: Eosinophilic Esophagitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Updated International Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Eosinophilic Esophagitis (2018)

criteria.description: Symptoms of esophageal dysfunction (dysphagia, food impaction, heartburn, chest pain)
Esophageal biopsies showing >= 15 eosinophils per high-power field
Mucosal eosinophilia isolated to the esophagus (not present in stomach/duodenum)
Endoscopic features (rings, furrows, exudates, edema, strictures)
Personal or family history of atopy (asthma, eczema, allergic rhinitis)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Both major criteria required: symptoms of esophageal dysfunction AND >= 15 eos/hpf on esophageal biopsies. Secondary causes of esophageal eosinophilia should be excluded.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: PPI-responsive esophageal eosinophilia is now considered part of the EoE spectrum and not a separate entity.

pathognomonic.notes: Most common presenting symptom in adults
Food bolus obstruction requiring emergency endoscopic removal

common.notes: Slow eating, excessive chewing, avoiding certain textures

occasional.notes: More common presentation in pediatric population

laboratory: Elevated serum IgE in ~70% of patients
imaging: Barium swallow may show ringed esophagus (feline esophagus), strictures, or narrow-caliber esophagus
EndoFLIP may demonstrate reduced esophageal distensibility
genetic: Polymorphisms in TSLP gene associated with increased risk
Variants in eotaxin-3 (CCL26) locus linked to susceptibility
CAPN14 gene variants associated with disease
other: Endoscopy: linear furrows, white exudates/plaques, concentric rings (trachealization), edema, strictures
EoE Endoscopic Reference Score (EREFS) for standardized grading
Biopsies should be taken from proximal and distal esophagus (at least 6 biopsies)

distinguishingFeatures: GERD responds well to PPIs with complete eosinophil resolution
GERD eosinophilia is typically distal only
GERD lacks endoscopic features of rings/furrows
EGE involves stomach/intestinal eosinophilia beyond esophagus
EGE may present with ascites or intestinal obstruction
Achalasia causes dysphagia to both solids and liquids equally

redFlags: Acute food impaction requiring emergency endoscopy
Signs of esophageal perforation (severe chest pain, subcutaneous emphysema)
Significant weight loss or failure to thrive in children
Rapidly progressive dysphagia suggesting stricture formation
references: Dellon ES, et al. Updated International Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Eosinophilic Esophagitis. Gastroenterology. 2018;155(4):1022-1033.
Lucendo AJ, et al. Guidelines on eosinophilic esophagitis: evidence-based statements and recommendations. United European Gastroenterol J. 2017;5(3):335-358.

Hirano I, et al. AGA Institute and the Joint Task Force on Allergy-Immunology Practice Parameters Clinical Guidelines for the Management of Eosinophilic Esophagitis. Gastroenterology. 2020;158(6):1776-1786.
